data.title: Vital Farms Introduces a Higher Standard for Free-Range Eggs Through Limited Pilot at Select Target Retail Stores
data.description:
Vital Farms () announced today the pilot launch of Vital Farms Free-Range eggs, which are expected to arrive in select Target retail stores across the South and Southeast beginning this week.

This limited test is designed to explore how Vital Farms can reach more households with a high-quality product at a more accessible suggested retail price point of less than $5 per carton, while maintaining its commitment to transparency and animal welfare.

Introducing A New Vital Farms Standard

“Free-range” is one of the most familiar terms in the egg aisle, but the standard itself doesn’t consistently tell consumers what they are actually buying. Compared with many other free-range products, the new Vital Farms Free-Range standard sets a higher bar for animal welfare in several meaningful areas: time outside, better land with living vegetation and shade, and barns designed to make it easier for hens to head outdoors. And like every carton of Vital Farms eggs, each carton can be traced back to the farm where the eggs were laid through the company’s “See The Farm” program.

This new Vital Farms standard for free-range reflects Vital Farms’ commitments to animal care, product quality, and transparency. Vital Farms loves hearing from consumers with questions. Visit vitalfarms.com/contact for details on how to call, text, direct message or write, or visit Vital Farms’ Frequently Asked Questions page to learn more.

Living Within Vital Farms’ Values and Testing Something New

“With Vital Farms Free-Range, we’re testing how we can bring more households a high-quality egg at a more accessible price point, while staying true to who we are and keeping hens’ quality of life front and center,” said Heather Mace, Vital Farms Vice President, Brand. “Our goal is to learn all we can, understand consumer appetite and grow the right way. Reaching more households gives us the opportunity to create more positive impact for our stakeholders while continuing to raise the standards in the egg aisle.”

Vital Farms Free-Range eggs are expected to be available beginning this week at select Target retail stores across the South and Southeast. For more information on where to find Vital Farms eggs, please visit: https://vitalfarms.com/where-to-buy/

ABOUT VITAL FARMS:

Vital Farms () is a Certified B Corporation that offers a range of ethically produced foods nationwide. Started on a single farm in Austin, Texas, in 2007, Vital Farms is now a national consumer brand that works with 600 small farms and is the leading U.S. brand of pasture-raised eggs by retail dollar sales. Vital Farms’ ethics are exemplified by its focus on the humane treatment of farm animals and sustainable farming practices. In addition, as a Delaware public benefit corporation, Vital Farms prioritizes the long-term benefits of each of its stakeholders, including farmers and suppliers, customers and consumers, communities and the environment, and crew members and stockholders. Vital Farms’ products, including shell eggs, hard-boiled eggs, and liquid whole eggs, are sold in more than 24,000 stores nationwide. Vital Farms pasture-raised eggs can also be found on menus at hundreds of foodservice operators across the country. For more information, visit https://vitalfarms.com.

data.title: Transocean Ltd. Files 8K - Other Events >RIG
data.description:
Transocean Ltd. (RIG) filed a Form 8K - Other Events - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on October 23, 2026.

As previously announced, on February 9, 2026, Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation ("Transocean") and Valaris Limited, an exempted company limited by shares incorporated under the laws of Bermuda ("Valaris"), entered into a Business Combination Agreement (the "Agreement"). The Agreement provides that, among other things and upon the terms and subject to the conditions thereof, Transocean will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris (the "Valaris Shares") in exchange for 15.235 shares of Transocean per Valaris Share (the "Business Combination"), pursuant to a court-sanctioned scheme of Arrangement (the "Scheme of Arrangement") between Valaris and the shareholders of Valaris (the "Valaris Shareholders"), pursuant to section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda, as amended (the "Companies Act").

On October 14, 2026, Transocean and Valaris filed a joint definitive proxy statement on Schedule 14A with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Proxy Statement") in connection with the (i) extraordinary general meeting (the "Transocean Meeting") of the shareholders of Transocean (the "Transocean Shareholders") at which the Transocean Shareholders will vote on certain matters related to the Business Combination and a proposal unrelated to the Business Combination to amend Transocean's Articles of Association, and (ii) special court-ordered meeting (the "Valaris Court Meeting") of Valaris Shareholders at which the Valaris Shareholders will vote on the Scheme of Arrangement and certain matters related to the Business Combination. Both the Transocean Meeting and the Valaris Court Meeting are scheduled to be held on November 24, 2026.

Subject to approval by the Transocean Shareholders of the requisite matters related to the Business Combination at the Transocean Meeting and approval by the Valaris Shareholders of the Scheme of Arrangement at the Valaris Court Meeting, in accordance with the Agreement Valaris will make an application to the Supreme Court of Bermuda (the "Bermuda Court"), for an order sanctioning the Scheme of Arrangement in accordance with section 99 of the Companies Act (the "Sanction Hearing").

The Sanction Hearing has been scheduled to be held on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Bermuda time) at Commercial Court, 2nd Floor, Government Administration Building, 30 Parliament Street, Hamilton HM12, Bermuda. Valaris Shareholders of record may appear in person or by counsel at the Sanction Hearing.

If the Bermuda Court grants the sanction order and sanctions the Scheme of Arrangement at the Sanction Hearing, Transocean anticipates that (i) all conditions to the consummation of the Business Combination will be satisfied and (ii) the Business Combination will be consummated on or about December 1, 2026.

data.title: Expion Energy Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >XPON
data.description:
Expion Energy Inc. (XPON) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on October 23, 2026.

Amendment and Restatement of Private Placement

Original Private Placement Transaction

As previously reported, on August 21, 2026, Expion Energy, Inc. (the "Company") entered into a securities purchase agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") with the purchasers identified on the signature pages thereto (the "Purchasers") pursuant to which the Company issued and sold to the Purchasers (i) 8% Convertible Debentures Due August 21, 2029 in the aggregate principal amount of $9,000,000 (the "Convertible Debentures"), which originally would have automatically converted into 9,000 shares of a series of preferred stock (the "Preferred Stock") to be designated the Series A-1 8% Convertible Preferred Stock (the "Series A-1 Preferred Stock") upon receiving stockholder approval of, and filing, a certificate of designation with the Nevada Secretary of State, and (ii) Common Stock Purchase Warrants (the "Warrants") to purchase up to 2,117,219 shares of the Company's common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the "Common Stock"). The Series A-1 Preferred Stock would have subsequently been convertible into shares of Common Stock on the terms set forth in the certificate of designation that was subject to stockholder approval.

Pursuant to the original Purchase Agreement, subject to receiving stockholder approval, and the filing of an applicable certificate of designation with the Nevada Secretary of State, the Purchasers would have been able to also elect to purchase additional shares of Preferred Stock (the "AIR Preferred Stock") with an aggregate stated value of up to $91,000,000, representing 91,000 additional shares of AIR Preferred Stock, at any time within 18 months following the effective date defined in the original Purchase Agreement. Such AIR Preferred Stock would have had substantially similar terms to the Series A-1 Preferred Stock issuable upon conversion of the Convertible Debentures.

Amendment and Restatement of Private Placement Transaction Documents

On October 22, 2026, the Company and the Purchasers entered into an amendment and restatement of the Purchase Agreement ("Amended and Restated Purchase Agreement"), and an amendment and restatement of the Convertible Debentures (the "Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures"), such that the Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures are now convertible into shares of Common Stock at an initial conversion price of $4.25 (subject to adjustment as described therein), which is equal to what the initial conversion price of the Series A-1 Preferred Stock would have been. The Company also amended and restated the Warrants (the "Amended and Restated Warrants") and the Registration Rights Agreement (the "Amended and Restated Registration Rights Agreement"). In addition, pursuant to the Amended and Restated Purchase Agreement, instead of AIR Preferred Stock, the Purchasers may now elect to purchase, at any time within 18 months following the effective date defined in the Amended and Restated Purchase Agreement, additional Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures (the "AIR Convertible Debentures") up to an aggregate principal amount of $91,000,000, which shall be convertible into shares of Common Stock (the "Additional Investment Right"). At each additional closing of the sale of AIR Convertible Debentures pursuant to an exercise of the Additional Investment Right, the AIR Convertible Debentures will be issued with substantially similar terms to the Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures, but in each case with a different original issuance date, maturity date and conversion price, and not including any provision permitting or requiring conversion at a price below the Floor Price (as defined below).

The foregoing transactions are collectively referred to as the "Private Placement". Unless specifically defined herein, or unless the context requires otherwise, capitalized terms used herein have the meanings set forth in the Amended and Restated Purchase Agreement.

Five Narrow Lane, LP ("FNL") was the lead Purchaser in the Private Placement. The Company's former Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board, Joseph Hammer, serves as a managing member of the general partner of FNL and may be deemed to share voting and dispositive power over the shares of Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures and AIR Convertible Debentures, and upon exercise of the Amended and Restated Warrants. The Private Placement (including the Amended and Restated Purchase Agreement, Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures, Amended and Restated Warrants and Amended and Restated Registration Rights Agreement) was approved by the disinterested members of the Company's board of directors.

Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures and AIR Convertible Debentures

The Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures and AIR Convertible Debentures are the direct, unsecured debt obligations of the Company and mature three years after their respective original issuance dates.

The Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures and AIR Convertible Debentures accrue interest on the aggregate unconverted and then outstanding principal amount at the Applicable Federal Rate as of the original issue date of the Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures and AIR Convertible Debentures, as applicable, and increasing to 8% per annum commencing on the first anniversary of the original issue date of the Amended and Restated Convertible Debentures and AIR Convertible Debentures, as applicable, payable quarterly on January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1, and on their respective maturity dates, payable in cash, or at the Company's option, in duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable registered shares of Common Stock, or a combination thereof, at an interest conversion rate equal to the lesser of (a) the conversion price, or (b) 90% of the arithmetic average of the three lowest daily volume weighted average prices during the five trading days prior to the applicable interest payment date, provided that the interest conversion rate shall not be less than the Floor Price. data.title: Delivery Firm Instacart Reportedly Explores Sale Options With Uber, DoorDash As Potential Buyers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Instacart has hired an investment bank to review its strategic options and has held preliminary takeover talks with major competitors Uber and DoorDash. 
  • With a market value of roughly $12 billion, the firm's acquisition price could be between $16 billion and $17 billion, The Information reported.
  • Any potential transaction is expected to face intense regulatory investigation due to antitrust concerns over overlapping market share in food and grocery delivery. 

Instacart (CART) is actively exploring a potential sale, engaging financial advisers and holding preliminary discussions with prospective buyers, including rivals DoorDash (DASH) and Uber (UBER).

The move could mark the conclusion of the grocery delivery pioneer’s 14-year run in which it played a central role in supplying households during pandemic-era lockdowns. The stock currently holds a market capitalization of approximately $12 billion.

A standard takeover premium of 30% to 40%—typical for public tech company acquisitions—could price a buyout in the range of $16 billion to $17 billion. However, discussions remain ongoing, and there is no guarantee that a definitive agreement will be reached, The Information reported.

CART stock gained about 9% on Friday and slipped 0.5% after-hours.

Regulatory Obstacles Ahead

Any proposed takeover of Instacart is expected to draw substantial scrutiny from antitrust authorities. Because potential suitors like DoorDash and Uber already operate established grocery delivery services, combining with a direct rival would trigger close regulatory oversight.

Antitrust officials under the current Trump administration have demonstrated a willingness to approve corporate deals provided certain conditions are met, such as requiring companies to divest specific assets. Still, direct horizontal mergers among dominant market players face rigorous scrutiny.

This is not the first time Instacart has contemplated a takeover. In 2021, when the company was privately valued at $39 billion, it held preliminary sale talks with DoorDash that could have valued the business at $40 billion to $50 billion. Those negotiations ultimately collapsed due to concerns over obtaining antitrust approval from Biden administration regulators.

Instacart Financial Performance

Instacart listed its shares publicly in 2023 at a $10 billion valuation, following a post-pandemic slowdown in consumer delivery demand. While its stock price has grown 70% since its public debut, its top-line expansion has lagged larger industry competitors despite its expansion into digital advertising.

Instacart recorded annual revenue growth of 11% in both 2024 and 2025, down from 19% in 2023. By comparison, DoorDash achieved a 28% revenue increase in 2025, while Uber’s total revenue climbed 18% during the same period, bolstered by its core ride-hailing operations. Increased competition from e-commerce giant Amazon (AMZN), which continues to scale its own grocery operations, has also put pressure on Instacart's market dominance.

Broader Sector Consolidation

DoorDash has expanded its footprint through international acquisitions, buying European delivery service Wolt for $8 billion in 2022, then acquiring British delivery provider Deliveroo and hospitality software platform SevenRooms last year.

Similarly, Uber has recently struck deals to acquire European firm Delivery Hero for roughly $15 billion and workplace catering provider Fooda.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

CART stock has gained about 23% year-to-date.

On October 14, 2026, Valaris and Transocean filed a joint definitive proxy statement on Schedule 14A with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Proxy Statement") in connection with the (i) special court-ordered meeting of Valaris (the "Valaris Court Meeting"), at which the Valaris Shareholders will vote on, among other matters related to the Business Combination, the Scheme of Arrangement and (ii) extraordinary general meeting (the "Transocean Meeting") of shareholders of Transocean (the "Transocean Shareholders") at which the Transocean Shareholders will vote on certain matters related to the Business Combination. Both the Valaris Court Meeting and the Transocean Meeting are scheduled to be held on November 24, 2026.

The Sanction Hearing has been scheduled to be held on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Bermuda time) at Commercial Court, 2nd Floor, Government Administration Building, 30 Parliament Street, Hamilton HM12, Bermuda. data.title: Fujitsu implements multi-AI agent infrastructure to enhance product information management for MISUMI Group
data.description:
KAWASAKI, Japan, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Fujitsu Limited today announced that it has implemented a multi-AI agent infrastructure for the product information management business of MISUMI Group Inc. (MISUMI). Building on the operation platform of its business model Uvance[1], Fujitsu leveraged "Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS"[2] to establish a system that supports the entire process, from data collection and pre-processing to AI-driven generation, evaluation, and final human verification. MISUMI began operating this new workflow in October.

This workflow targets tens of thousands of products listed on MISUMI's e-commerce site. By creating an operational model where humans and AI collaborate, the project aims to improve both the efficiency and quality of product information management.

The platform was built in approximately 2.5 months. This rapid deployment was achieved through an agile development process, where Fujitsu's Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) worked closely with MISUMI's business personnel to integrate professional operational judgment criteria and verification methods directly into the AI agents.

Background

As MISUMI has expanded its product offerings, the volume of data requiring registration, including product category classifications and technical specifications, has grown substantially. Registering new products and series typically required manual, time-consuming processes across multiple internal and external systems. These manual dependencies created bottlenecks, delaying product launches on the e-commerce site and presenting challenges in maintaining data consistency and quality. To address these issues, Fujitsu is leveraging Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS to transform the business processes through AI integration.

Project Highlights

1. Rapid implementation

Fujitsu quickly established a data utilization foundation and AI execution environment by leveraging Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS. In addition, Fujitsu's Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) worked in close cooperation with business personnel at MISUMI to incorporate their expertise, such as operational judgment criteria and verification methods, into the AI agents. The team also built a workflow that integrates a confirmation and approval process by human operators. Through this agile development approach, the multi-AI agent platform was successfully applied to actual business operations in just 2.5 months after the project began.

2. Quality enhancement through AI collaboration

The workflow utilizes nine AI agents, each with distinct roles such as generating series names, suggesting categories, extracting specifications, and checking for restricted characters. These agents mutually evaluate the validity of their outputs, while final human approval ensures accuracy and consistency across the catalog.

3. Focus on high-value operations

Automating routine registration and verification tasks significantly reduces the administrative burden on staff. This allows employees to shift their focus toward higher-value activities, such as strategic decision-making and business process improvements.

Future Plans

Fujitsu will continue to collaborate with MISUMI to gradually expand the scope of the developed data models and AI-driven workflows. The next phases will include end-to-end management from initial product data ingestion from suppliers to master data management, with the goal of further automating the entire workflow through integration with peripheral systems. Fujitsu remains committed to supporting business transformation in the manufacturing sector through its Uvance model, driving faster time-to-market and increased industrial competitiveness.

data.title: Defensive-led market breadth is a warning sign, not a win - Carson
data.description:
Carson Group is warning investors that the long-awaited expansion in market breadth may have arrived with a painful catch—it's being driven by defensive sectors while AI stocks are in freefall.

On Thursday, 324 of 500 S&P 500 companies increased, with the median stock climbing 1.09%, Carson noted in a blog post published Friday. Yet the S&P 500 itself fell 1.36%, technology plunged 3.3%, and the Goldman Sachs Broad AI Index dropped 6.01%. Nine of 11 sectors beat the index, with defensive plays—staples , utilities , and health care —leading the way.

The shift has been dramatic. On June 22, AI stocks were outperforming non-AI stocks by 49 percentage points year-to-date. That lead has collapsed to just 4.8 points.

Through Thursday, non-AI stocks have outperformed AI by over 28 percentage points in the second half of 2026.

The concentration problem is acute. Technology alone represents 38% of the S&P 500, and adding Alphabet , Meta , Amazon , and Tesla pushes AI-linked exposure past 51%, Carson said. In the first half of 2026, when the S&P 500 returned 10.2%, the AI basket contributed 75% of that gain despite averaging only 37% of index weight.

That dynamic has reversed. In the second half, the AI basket—now 39% of the index—has subtracted 1.7 percentage points from S&P 500 returns, while non-AI stocks contributed 4.2 points.

Carson pointed out that that rotation marked the end of the late 1990s tech bubble and warned that if the current pattern persists, it could signal the end of both the AI wave and the broader bull market.
